messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A temporary fix used to expose a fault. the one part you expected to use turns out to be missing. Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i put the loose screw back on, then put the loose screw back on again. the fault keeps shifting. i put the loose bracket back on, but the screw stays. i put the bracket back on, but the loose screw stays. i put the bracket back on again, but the loose screw keeps shifting."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "you put the fault on the step. you look at the missing part. “wrong.” you put the entire thing back. you keep the wrong part. the repair lasts longer."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I rub my palm and put the broken edge down. \"Missing fault part,\" I say. I scrape the gap with my thumbnail, then put the repaired part back. I take one bright breath and mark the fault with my finger."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "i put the faulty piece back on the shelf. the one missing takes the place of the one i thought. i put the rest of the repair in the drawer. the fault stays missing."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i put the faulty part back in the corner, then touch the edge with my thumbnail. the fault stays visible, so i put the rest back in its place. i write the missing part on a scrap and put it back in the corner again. this time, i use the thumb to trim the edge."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i put the loose part beside the one I found. the fault stays. i leave the rest where it is. the one I expected can wait another day."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "I put the faulty part back on the bench and check the joint with my thumb. I leave the old part beside it, then try the new one once. If it still fails, I leave it beside the drawer and leave the part beside the drawer label."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "I tap the joint once and leave the old piece beside it. I tap the same spot again. I turn the old one once and put it back."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "1. check the missing part. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. check the tinkered watch. 4. check the tinkered piece. 5. check the shelf. 6. check the tinkered piece twice. 7. put the repair in a clean cloth. 8. check the watch. slow. 9. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i write the fault on the receipt, then check the original one. i leave it where it is, then test the missing one. i leave the temporary fix behind and write the exact date on the receipt."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i put the faulty part down and hold it against the wall. “i did not,” i say, then move the rest. “i did not. i did not. i did not. i do not know why it did not work.” i keep my hand off the wall and watch the faulty part."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "I take the loose bolt. “not sure.” i bend it with my thumb. i pocket the rust and leave the bolt loose. then i move the loose part back and check the new place. maybe the fault is still there."}]
